value.body: A master's degree from a university outside India — called an MS in the US and an MSc or MEng in the UK, Europe, Canada and Australia. Programmes usually last one to two years and are taught in English. Common choices include computer science, data science, engineering, business analytics, finance and public health.

items.label: Course length
items.note: Often 2 years in the US and Canada; often 1 year in the UK and Ireland

items.label: Indian students abroad (higher education)
items.note: Down from ~13.3 lakh a year earlier; across all degree levels
items.source: Ministry of External Affairs, Parliament reply (as reported)

items.label: Indian students in the US
items.note: All levels; India is the largest sending country

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A bachelor's degree (usually 4 years for the US; many 3-year degrees are accepted in the UK and elsewhere). You apply to each university directly with transcripts, a statement of purpose and recommendation letters. Many programmes ask for an English test — IELTS, TOEFL or PTE — and some, mostly in the US, ask for the GRE (or GMAT for business programmes). After an offer, you apply for a student visa, which needs proof of funds.

value.title: At a glance
items: Total cost (tuition plus living) varies a great deal by country, city and university; many students rely on education loans.
Visa and post-study work rules change often — Canada, for example, has capped new study permits since 2024.
Funding is less common at master's level than at PhD level; assistantships and scholarships exist but are competitive.
A master's abroad can lead to work in that country, a PhD, or a return to India.
